newsitem.title: USA: UPS-union talks resume on U.S. strike.
newsitem.headline: UPS-union talks resume on U.S. strike.

text.p: Talks resumed Monday between United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union, the 15th day of a strike that has crippled small package deliveries and cost the company $650 million in lost revenue.

"We're working very hard to make this strike part of history," federal mediator John Calhoun Wells said as he arrived shortly before the talks began. "Hopefully that's going to happen sooner than later."
Some 185,000 UPS workers went on strike Aug. 4 to demand full-time status for more part-time staff and in protest against a proposal to change their pension fund arrangements.
After marathon talks over the weekend, UPS chairman James Kelly said on Monday that a settlement was closer, but he forecast the strike could last much longer if negotiations broke off this week.
"We are indeed closer than we were four days ago, but there are still some very difficult issues for them (negotiators) to discuss today," Kelly told CNN.
White House spokesman Barry Toiv said President Bill Clinton wanted a settlement.
"He continues to urge the parties to work hard to bridge their remaining differences," he added.
